title: Dominant finite-type affine charts with compatible function-field maps
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme], dominant in the sense that $f(X)$ is dense in $S$, and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $S$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For every $x\in X$, with $s=f(x)$, there exist nonempty affine open neighbourhoods $s\in U\subseteq S$ and $x\in V\subseteq X$ with $f(V)\subseteq U$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], such that $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_S)$ is a Noetherian domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$ is a domain and a finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and the ring map $\varphi:A\to B$ induced by $f$ is injective. One can choose $U$ from any prescribed affine covering of $S$ by Noetherian coordinate rings, and then choose $V$ inside $f^{-1}(U)$.

Write $\eta_S,\eta_X$ for the generic points [def-sc-generic-point] and $R(S)=\mathcal O_{S,\eta_S}$, $R(X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta_X}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then $\eta_S\in U$, $\eta_X\in V$, their primes in $A,B$ are $(0)$, and $f(\eta_X)=\eta_S$. The generic germ maps $g_S:A\to R(S)$ and $g_X:B\to R(X)$ identify $R(S)$ and $R(X)$ with the fraction fields $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, namely fields of fractions with nonzero denominators. If $f_\eta^\sharp:R(S)\to R(X)$ is the map on generic stalks, these identifications satisfy
$$f_\eta^\sharp(g_S(a)/g_S(b))=g_X(\varphi(a))/g_X(\varphi(b))\quad(a,b\in A,\ b\ne0).$$
In particular $f_\eta^\sharp$ is the fraction-field embedding extending $\varphi$, rather than an unspecified field embedding.

proof.text: Choose a member $U$ of the prescribed affine covering of $S$ containing $s$. Such a covering exists by [pqf-def-locnoeth]; its coordinate ring $A$ is Noetherian by the condition on the prescribed covering. For this particular affine $U$, the definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives an affine open covering of $f^{-1}(U)$ by spectra of finite type $A$-algebras. Choose a member $V$ containing $x$ and put $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$. Both opens are nonempty because they contain the specified points. The definition [def-pc-integral-scheme] makes $A$ and $B$ domains. The structural map of the chosen $A$-algebra $B$ is precisely the restriction of the section pullback of $f$, denoted $\varphi$. This proves the chart-selection clauses without changing the prescribed covering.

source.place: Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), (1)--(4), applied over the chosen affine; Tag 02JU (lemma-dimension-formula), affine reduction

proof.text: For either pair $(T,W)=(S,U)$ or $(X,V)$, integrality implies irreducibility by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. By [def-weil-irreducible-components], the nonempty open $W$ is dense: otherwise the two proper closed sets $\overline W$ and $T\setminus W$ would cover $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] (2), the point $(0)$ is generic in the affine domain spectrum $W$. Its closure in $T$ therefore contains $W$ and hence all of $T$, so it is a generic point as defined in [def-sc-generic-point]. Every generic point of $T$ belongs to $W$, since otherwise its closure would lie in the proper closed set $T\setminus W$. Its prime $\mathfrak p$ in $W$ must be zero: the closure $V(\mathfrak p)$ is all of $\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_T)$, so it contains the prime $(0)$ and $\mathfrak p\subseteq(0)$. Thus the generic point is unique and the points $\eta_S,\eta_X$ belong to $U,V$ with primes $(0)$.

source.place: Tag 0CC1 (lemma-dominant-between-integral), proof: generic points correspond to zero primes; Properties Tag 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral)

proof.text: For an open $W\subseteq T$ and $t\in W$, restriction identifies $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ with $\mathcal O_{W,t}$ and preserves germs of sections on $W$. Indeed, in the germ description of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], replace a representative $(N,a)$ by $(N\cap W,a|_{N\cap W})$. Conversely a neighbourhood in $W$ is open in $T$, so its representative already defines a germ on $T$. The equality criterion for germs makes these maps inverse and shows that they preserve addition and multiplication. To check the morphism comparison, let $f(V)\subseteq U$, $t\in V$, and represent an input germ by $a\in\mathcal O_S(N)$ with $f(t)\in N\subseteq U$. The original stalk map sends it to the germ of $f^\sharp_N(a)$ on $f^{-1}(N)$. Restricting this section to $V\cap f^{-1}(N)$ gives exactly the pullback under $f|_V:V\to U$, by the restriction compatibility in [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Thus the restricted and original stalk maps agree under the open-stalk identifications, on every germ.

source.place: Tag 01IJ (definition-scheme), open subschemes; stalks as germs in Sheaves Tag 0078

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] (2) to the domains $A$ and $B$ and their zero primes from Step 2. Its fraction-field identifications use the germ maps from global sections. Step 3 consequently identifies $R(S)=\mathcal O_{S,\eta_S}$ and $R(X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta_X}$, with exactly the maps $g_S$ and $g_X$ in the statement, as fields of fractions of $A$ and $B$. In particular the germ maps are injective, all nonzero denominators become invertible, and each element of either generic stalk is a quotient of two such germs.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), (1), (6), at the zero prime; Morphisms Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions), integral case

proof.text: Continuity of $f$ gives $f(X)\subseteq\overline{\{f(\eta_X)\}}$: the inverse image of any closed set containing $f(\eta_X)$ is closed and contains $\eta_X$, hence contains $X$. Dominance then gives $S=\overline{f(X)}\subseteq\overline{\{f(\eta_X)\}}$. Thus $f(\eta_X)$ is generic in $S$ in the sense of [def-sc-generic-point], and uniqueness proved in Step 2 gives $f(\eta_X)=\eta_S$. Here continuity is part of the underlying map of a scheme morphism [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]; no openness or surjectivity of $f$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0CC1 (lemma-dominant-between-integral), (1) implies (2), with the elementary closure argument written out

proof.text: The affine restriction $V\to U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For $Q=(0)\subset B$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] says that its image prime is $\varphi^{-1}(Q)$. By Steps 2 and 5 this image is $(0)\subset A$. Hence $\ker\varphi=\varphi^{-1}((0))=(0)$ and $\varphi$ is injective. The same cited statement gives the map $\varphi_0:A_{(0)}\to B_{(0)}$, $a/b\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(b)$, as the actual affine stalk map, with its commuting germ square. Let $i_A:A_{(0)}\xrightarrow{\sim}R(S)$ and $i_B:B_{(0)}\xrightarrow{\sim}R(X)$ be the identifications of Steps 3 and 4, so $i_A(a/1)=g_S(a)$ and $i_B(c/1)=g_X(c)$. The representative calculation of Step 3 identifies the original stalk map with the affine one, giving $f_\eta^\sharp\circ i_A=i_B\circ\varphi_0$. Evaluating at $a/1$ proves $f_\eta^\sharp(g_S(a))=g_X(\varphi(a))$ for every $a\in A$. Thus the germ square remains the square for the original morphism after both open-stalk identifications.

source.place: Tag 0CC1 (lemma-dominant-between-integral), (2) implies (4) and proof; Schemes Tags 01HY (lemma-morphism-into-affine-where-point-goes), 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine)

proof.text: For clarity, the commuting germ square of Step 6 reads $f_\eta^\sharp(g_S(a))=g_X(\varphi(a))$ for every $a\in A$. If $b\ne0$, injectivity of $\varphi$ and $g_X$ gives $g_X(\varphi(b))\ne0$. Since $f_\eta^\sharp$ is a unital ring map between the fields of Step 4, applying it to the equation $g_S(b)g_S(b)^{-1}=1$ shows that it preserves this inverse. Therefore $f_\eta^\sharp(g_S(a)/g_S(b))=g_X(\varphi(a))/g_X(\varphi(b))$. Every element of $R(S)$ has this form by Step 4, so this formula uniquely determines the map extending $\varphi$. It is an embedding: if a nonzero field element mapped to zero, multiplying by the image of its inverse would give $1=0$ in the field $R(X)$.
